paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness bundle: agent status in the macOS menu bar (SwiftBar) — pending approvals, running
tasks, finished tasks, plus system notifications.
# DSH Status Notifier

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle that puts your agent's live
status in the macOS menu bar — so you ca

n see pending approvals and finished tasks without switching back to the
Harness window.
## What it shows
| Menu bar | Meaning |

| `⚠ 1` (orange) | A permission request is waiting for your approval |
| `● 1` (blue) | A task is ru

nning |
| `✓ 1` (green) | A task finished less than 30 minutes ago |
| `○ 空闲` (gray) | Idle |
Clicking the item opens a dropdown listing the sessions behind each state; any row (or the "打开 DeepS

eek Harness"
row) brings the Harness window back. It refreshes every 5 seconds.
It also fires macOS system notifications while the page is away (window hidden or unfocused), and th

rough
`osascript` when the window is closed but the Host keeps running — so a long task can finish w

hile you are in
another app and you still get told. The two notification paths never double-alert: t

he Host only notifies when no
page is connected.
## How it works
Two halves, one bundle:

- **Host half** (`index.js`) runs in the DSH Host process:
- observes durable, order-independent sig

nals — `session/event` with `approval/asked` / `approval/decided`
(the approval audit pair appended

by the Approval service) and `agent/status` running↔idle transitions;
- renders a SwiftBar script (`

dsh-status.5s.sh`) plus its output into the plugin folder; the rendered state
files live **outside**

the plugin folder, so SwiftBar never mistakes them for plugins;
- falls back to `osascript` notific

ations when no page is connected.
- **Client half** (`client.js`) runs in the Web GUI: watches the f

ramework's own `uiSession.sessionStatus`
(running / pendingInteraction / completionUnread) and fires
browser notifications when the window is away.
## Requirements

- macOS with SwiftBar (`brew install --cask swiftbar`)
- DeepSeek Harness with plugin bundle support
## Installation

1. Clone this repository anywhere, or copy the folder into your workspace.
2. Install the bundle in

DSH — Plugin Manager → install local bundle, or ask your agent to run `plugin_manager`
`install_bund

le` with this directory as the target.
3. Make SwiftBar watch the folder:
- create `~/.swiftbar` and

point SwiftBar's Preferences → General → Plugin Folder at it, or
- keep SwiftBar's own folder and w

rite its path into the first line of `~/.dsh/swiftbar-dir.txt`.
4. Restart DeepSeek Harness so the H
ost half loads. The menu bar item appears within a few seconds.
## Configuration
| Variable / file | Purpose |
| `DSH_SWIFTBAR_DIR` | SwiftBar plugin folder (else `~/.dsh/swiftbar-dir.txt`, else `~/.swiftbar`) |

| `~/.dsh/swiftbar-dir.txt` | First line: the plugin folder path |
| `DSH_SWIFTBAR_STATE_DIR` | Whe
re rendered state files go (default `~/.dsh/swiftbar-state`) |
## Development
`test-render.mjs` runs the Host half against a stubbed Cordis context, simulates approval / running

/ idle
events, and checks the rendered SwiftBar output and the legacy-file cleanup:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Notes and limits

- The menu bar item is a SwiftBar script: SwiftBar must be running for the item to appear.
- Clickin
g a row brings the Harness window back; deep-linking straight into a specific session is not support

ed
yet.
- State directories are resolved when the plugin loads; after changing them, restart DeepSee
State directories are resolved when the plugin loads; after changing them, restart DeepSeek Harness.
